title: Circumference Avatar Tape  (ver. 5.1.4)
content: ### Related articles [Linear Avatar Tape](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358281835673) [Attach to Avatar Tape](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358293301145) [Delete Avatar Tape](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358298422553) ### ### Objective Create a circumference baseline on avatars to improve accuracy in fit and draping. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Tape ▶ Circumference Avatar Tape 3D Toolbar ▶ Circumference Avatar Tape ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Tape ▶ Circumference Avatar Tape 3D Toolbar ▶ Circumference Avatar Tape 2. Click to make the beginning point of the tape at a desired place. → Blue dot appears and gets fixed. 3. title: MODULAR MODE: Edit Blocks
content: ### Objective Open and edit Patterns in provided Blocks from the Modular Configurator or replace them with your own. ### Location Modular Mode ▶ Block Editor ### Operation Edit Patterns 1\. Load Blocks from the Modular Configurator. 2\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode ▶ Block Editor 3\. Select a Block to edit in the list of the Block Editor. → Remaining Blocks are frozen. 4\. Modify it with the Edit Pattern tool. 5\. Once the modification is done, Simulate the according Block when the rest of the Blocks are still frozen. 6\. Once the modification is completed, reselect the selected Block. → All of the Blocks are activated again. Replace Patterns 1.Load Blocks from the Modular Configurator. 2\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode ▶ Block Editor 3\. Locate Patterns out of Block Boxes or delete them. → The Block Boxes remain in light grey. 4\. Add desired Garment files to substitute with. 5.Click and drag the Patterns that are just loaded to matching Block Boxes. → The Patterns are linked with the Block Boxes. 6\. Sew the Patterns to Block Boxes. 7\. Select the according Block in the Block Editor, freeze the rest, then Simulate. ※ Note: * Selected Blocks in the Block Editor are also selected in the 2D window. * Editing Pattern in the Modular Mode is the same as the Simulation Mode. Deleting a segment or a point in a Pattern also deletes Sewing Lines between the Pattern and the Block Box.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to guide users in editing and replacing Patterns within Blocks using the Modular Configurator's Block Editor.

title: 3D Free Sewing (VER4.2.0)
content: ### Objective In the 3D window, freely establish Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes/Lines. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Free Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ Free Sewing ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Free Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ Free Sewing → All sew-able segments are bolded. → All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. 2. Click, drag and double click on Pattern outline or Internal Shape/Line to establish the start and end points of the first half of the seam. 3. Similarly, click again on another Pattern outline or Internal Shape/Line to establish the start point of the second half of the seam. → Drag the mouse cursor as a blue point appears guiding the length of the first half of the seam. 4. The mouse cursor snaps to the blue guide point. 5. Be mindful to make the Directional Notches parallel to each other and click to complete the second half of the seam. ※ Note: * The face of the Directional Notch of a Sewing Line defers depending on the order of establishing the start and the end point of the Sewing Line. * Right click while establishing the Free Sewing Line to enter the desired length of the Sewing Line in the Create Sewing Line window. * Use the shortcut to establish M:N sewing lines. For more detail, please reference M:N Free Sewing. ※ Note: 3D Sewing Video
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for users to create and manipulate Sewing Lines on pattern outlines and internal shapes within a 3D environment.

title: Remeshing to Retopology (Selected)  (ver. 5.1.4)
content: ### Objective Remesh selected pattern and generate retopology lines along the remeshed polygon. ### Location Right-click pattern pop-up menu (3D window) → Remeshing to Retopology ### Operation 1. Click the menu specified in Location. 2. A polygon count input dialog will pop up. → Enter the desired number of polygons and click the Apply button. 3. The mesh of the selected patterns is rearranged into an aligned quad mesh. 4. Retopology lines are generated along the remeshed polygons. 5. To return to the previous status, right-click on the pattern and select 'Undo Remeshing' from the pop-up menu.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for using the Remesh feature to generate retopology lines on selected polygons in your 3D modeling software.

title: Fabric List Window
content: Default_Fabric is provided as default Fabric, and being displayed in the Fabric list. When editing Default_Fabric, the edited default Fabric maintains until reopen a garment or rerun a program. You can reset edited properties of Default_Fabric with > Right Click > Pop Up Menu.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide guidance on managing and resetting the Default_Fabric properties within the Fabric list for garment editing and program reruns.

title: Delete Avatar
content: ### Objective Select avatar and delete individually. ※ Note: Versions below ver2.5.0 only allow avatar deletion for all. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Delete Avatar 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Pop-up Menu (Right-click on Avatar) ▶ Delete Avatar ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Delete Avatar 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Pop-up Menu (Right-click on Avatar) ▶ Delete Avatar → The avatar is now being deleted. ※ Note: From ver2.5.0, deleted avatars can immediately be restored at Main Menu ▶ Edit ▶ Undo or Press (Ctrl+Z)

title: AVATAR CREATING MEASUREMENT: Height Measurement
content: ### Objective Take avatar's height measurements from the ground to the relevant points. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Measurement ▶ Height Measurement Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D window Toolbar) ▶ Measurement Toolbar ▶ (Hold left mouse button at least two seconds) ▶ Height Measurement ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Measurement ▶ Height Measurement Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D window Toolbar) ▶ Measurement Toolbar ▶ (Hold left mouse button at least two seconds) ▶ Height Measurement 2. Click a point to take the height measurement. 3. Double-click another point to end the height measurement. → A light-green colored rectangle indicating the ground automatically appears, and a green line connecting the ground and the clicked point appears to indicate the height.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for accurately measuring an avatar's height from the ground to specific points within a 3D environment.

title: BUTTON STYLE PROPERTIES: Button Size
content: ### Objective Adjust button sizes as desired. ### Location #### Before ver4.0.0 Object Browser ▶ Button Tab ▶ Property Editor ▶ Size #### After ver4.0.0 Object Browser ▶ Button Tab ▶ Property Editor ▶ Width/ Thickness/ Weight ### Operation #### Before ver4.0.0 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Select a button item in the Button Tab. → Its properties appear in the Property Editor. 2. Find the Size option and enter desired value. → The button size is now being adjusted and applied. #### After ver4.0.0 1. Navigate to the Object Browser and select the desired Button item from the button tab. → The selected button item's properties appear in the Property Editor. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Button Tab ▶ Property Editor ▶ Width/ Thickness/ Weight 3. Refer to the table below and adjust each option as needed. Option | Description ---|--- Width | Adjust button width. Thickness | Enter the desired value for button thickness. Weight | Enter the desired value for button weight in grams.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for adjusting button sizes in the Object Browser, detailing the process before and after version 4.0.0.

title: Delete All Overlapping Points
content: ### Objective Delete overlapping points on patterns/internal shapes (ver2.5.0). When cutting Patterns in Marvelous Designer, two Segment Points can be created very close to each other, below the minimum distance set by Marvelous Designer. When the aforementioned case happens, the respective Patterns cannot be moved nor edited, but can be resolved by deleting the overlapping points. ### Location Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) ▶ Delete All Overlapping Points ### Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) ▶ Delete All Overlapping Points → All overlapping points on Patterns and Internal Shapes are deleted.
content_description: This web page provides a straightforward guide on how to delete overlapping points in patterns and internal shapes within Marvelous Designer to ensure smooth editing and movement of your designs.

title: Duplicate as Button to Symmetric Pattern
content: ### Objective Duplicate buttons as buttonholes, or buttonholes as buttons, to its Symmetric Pattern. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button 2. Click on the button or buttonhole to be duplicated to its Symmetric Pattern. → The selected button or buttonhole is highlighted in yellow. 3. Right click on the selected button or buttonhole. → The right-click pop-up menu appears. 4. Depending on the selected item, select Duplicate as Button to Symmetric Pattern or Duplicate as Buttonhole to Symmetric Pattern. → The selected button or buttonhole is duplicated as a buttonhole or button, depending on the selected item, to its Symmetric Pattern.
content_description: This web page guides users through the process of duplicating buttons and buttonholes to their Symmetric Pattern using the 3D Toolbar.

title: Layer Clone
content: ### Objective Create an instance of the Pattern in its 3D state while sewing its Pattern outlines and Internal Lines to its instance's Pattern outlines and Internal Lines. Use the function to easily create padded jackets, collars, cuffs and other garments/details made with multiple layers of Patterns. ### Location Right Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Layer Clone (Over/Under) ### Operation 1. Select Transform Pattern tool or Edit Pattern tool. 2. Select the Patterns to be layer cloned. 3. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Layer Clone (Over) → The cloned Pattern is placed above the original Pattern. Right Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Layer Clone (Under) → The cloned Pattern is placed beneath the original Pattern. 4. Activate Simulation. → The cloned layer is simulated based on the option selected.
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for using the Layer Clone function to create and simulate 3D instances of garment patterns, enabling the design of layered clothing details like padded jackets, collars, and cuffs.

title: Copy Buttonhole Style
content: ### Objective Copy and modify a buttonhole in order to create a new buttonhole style or adjust its properties. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab ▶ Copy ### Operation 1. Navigate to the Object Browser and select an item in the buttonhole tab. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab ▶ Copy → A new buttonhole item with the same properties of the selected item is now being created.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for copying and modifying buttonholes to create new styles or adjust their properties.

title: ADD CUSTOM BUTTON AND BUTTONHOLE: Register Custom OBJ as Button
content: ### Objective Register a custom OBJ file as Button. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Register Button Property Editor ▶ Shape ▶ plus_button.png ### Operation #### #### Create Button OBJ Please check below requirements before registering an OBJ as a button. ※Required: * Position the face of an OBJ towards Y-axis. * Position the contact point of an OBJ where it should be attached to 3D garments at 0,0,0 (x,y,z) coordinates. * The unit of OBJs must be in mm. ※Recommended: * Please maintain the number of vertices of an OBJ below 1000 to avoid speed issues. * The distance between an OBJ and the ground should be 0. (You can adjust the distance in Marvelousdesigner. Button Property Setting ▶ Thread Length (cm)) #### Register Button OBJ 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. → Register Button window appears. 2. After setting the following options, Click OK. Name | Set the name of the button file. ---|--- Thumbnail | Apply the thumbnail of the button file. Button (ver. 11) | Set the properties for the button file to be registered. ※Note: If the OBJ shape is different for each button size, click the + button on the top right to register as buttons of various sizes. Size Name | Set the size name. OBJ | Load the OBJ file to be registered with the button. Width/Thickness/Weight | Set the width/thickness/weight of the button. Default Size | Set the size to be applied by default when changing with the button. → The registered button is saved in the path below. ▶ Assets ▶ Materials ▶ Hardware_and_Trims ▶ Button & Buttonhole ▶ Button #### Create Button OBJ by Thread Type 1. Set the Mesh name of the button to REN_BUTTON, REN_THREAD. 2. Create an OBJ for each thread type with the above MESH name. Set the name of the OBJ file for each thread type to *_Cross.obj, *_Parallel.obj , *_Square.obj. 3. Register the created OBJ file as a button. 4. Save the created *_Cross.btn, *_Parallel.btn , *_Square.btn files in the path below. C:\Users\Public\Documents\Marvelousdesigner\Assets\Materials\Hardware_and_Trims\Button & Buttonhole\Button 5. Run Marvelousdesigner and change the type of the thread in the button property window > Type > Thread Type.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for registering a custom OBJ file as a button in the Marvelous Designer software, ensuring proper setup and optimization for 3D garment design.

title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Open/Save Fabric
content: Save a commonly used fabric as a PSP file and reload it to use as needed. At Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Fabric, press Save to save and press Open to load the saved Fabric data.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for saving and reloading commonly used fabrics as PSP files using the Fabric Property Editor in Object Browser.

title: Delete Buttonhole Style
content: ### Objective Delete unnecessary buttonhole styles. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab 2. Select a buttonhole style to be deleted. 3. Press the Delete key on keyboard or right click on the buttonhole style and select Delete. → The selected buttonhole style is deleted.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for deleting unnecessary buttonhole styles from the Object Browser's Buttonhole Tab.

title: Merge
content: ### Objective Merge two Patterns in to a single Pattern. ### Location #### Pattern Outline Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern #### Sewing Line Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Edit Sewing 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Sewing ### Operation #### Pattern Outline 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern 2. Select two Pattern outlines which two Patterns are to be merged accordingly. ※ Note: When the Patterns are symmetrically linked, select the Pattern outline of the either Pattern. 3. Right click on the selected Pattern outlines to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Merge. → The selected two Patterns are merged based on the selected Pattern outlines. → The original Pattern outlines are changed to Baselines. #### Sewing Line 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Edit Sewing 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Sewing 2. Right click on the Sewing Line which the Patterns are merged accordingly. Then, select Merge. → The two Patterns sewn with the selected Sewing Line are merged based on the selected Sewing Line. → The original Pattern outlines are changed to Baselines.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for merging two pattern outlines and their corresponding sewing lines into a single cohesive pattern.

title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Adjust Collision Thickness
content: ### Objective Simulation thickness is invisible set property that represents the collision limit for Garments to result smooth Simulation. By default, the Simulation thickness from the Garment Pattern is set 1.5mm on each side, for a total of 3mm, and this value is adjustable as required. Lower the thickness value to work on Garments that are more likely to be form-fitting, or increase the thickness value to use as padding and etc. ※ Note: For the same reason, the default value of Avatar thickness (Skin Offset) is set for 3mm. For form-fitting Garments or accurate fitting measurement, it is recommended that Skin Offset is adjusted alongside the Simulation thickness. ### Location Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ Add'l Thickness-Collision ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ Add'l Thickness-Collision 2. Enter desired rendering thickness value. →The thickness is now being adjusted and applied.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on adjusting the simulation thickness property for garments to optimize collision limits and achieve smoother simulations.

title: Sewing Line Type
content: ### Objective Apply the Turned Sewing Line type setting to achieve a folded, two ply look. ![Sewing](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438733625881) ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Edit Sewing ▶ (Select Sewing Line) Property Editor ▶ Sewing Line Type 2D/3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Sewing ▶ (Select Sewing Line) Property Editor ▶ Sewing Line Type ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Edit Sewing ▶ (Select Sewing Line) Property Editor ▶ Sewing Line Type 2D/3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Sewing ▶ (Select Sewing Line) Property Editor ▶ Sewing Line Type 2. Select Turned. 3. Activate Simulation. → Double layered Patterns are sewn together crisp and flat.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for applying the Turned Sewing Line type setting to create a folded, two-ply look in your sewing projects.

title: CREATE CUSTOM BUTTON TEXTURE: Apply Custom Button Texture
content: ### Objective Apply custom button texture to buttons in Marvelous Designer. ### Location Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Diffuse Map ### Operation 1. Navigate to Object Browser ▶ Button Tab and select the button item to be edited. → The button item's properties appear in the Property Editor. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Diffuse Map → The file browser appears. 3. Locate and select the custom button texture and select Open. → The custom button texture is applied to the selected button item.
content_description: Learn how to apply a custom texture to buttons in Marvelous Designer by using the Property Editor to select and upload your desired diffuse map.

title: Delete Button Style
content: ### Objective Delete unnecessary button styles. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Button Tab ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Button Tab 2. Select a button style to be deleted. 3. Press Delete on keyboard or right click on the button style and select Delete option. → The selected button style is not deleted.
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for deleting unnecessary button styles in the Object Browser's Button Tab.

title: Create AI Bezier Curve
content: ### Objective Create curves in Marvelous Designer similarly how they are drawn in Adobe Illustrator (ver3.0.0). ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ Polygon or Internal Polygon/Line 2D Toolbar ▶ Polygon or Internal Polygon/Line ### Operation #### Create AI Curves 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ Polygon or Internal Polygon/Line 2D Toolbar ▶ Polygon or Internal Polygon/Line 2. Click and drag on the 2D window. The curve is created as the blue handle appears. → Continue to drag to adjust curvature. When the desired curvature is achieved, let go the mouse cursor. ![Proyecto](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438538047513) 3. To draw a straight line or change the direction of the curve, click on the point created at last. Then, continue to draw polygon or Internal Polygon/Line. #### Cancel Actions 1. To cancel all actions, hit Esc key or Ctrl + Z keys on the keyboard. → All the actions taken to create polygon or Internal Polygon/Line are undone. 2. To cancel the last step, hit Delete key or Backspace key on the keyboard. → The point created at last is undone.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide to creating curves in Marvelous Designer, mimicking the drawing techniques used in Adobe Illustrator.

title: Topstitch List Window
content: ### Objective It is possible to create, copy, apply and set a style in Topstitch list window. Without any extra setting, Default_Topstitch is applied as default. Once the Default_Topstitch style is modified, it lasts until rerun of the program and it cannot be deleted. ![Captura](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438627473945)
content_description: This web page provides guidance on creating, copying, and applying styles in the Topstitch list window, highlighting the use of the Default_Topstitch style and its persistent modifications.

title: Create 3D Garment Measure
content: ### Objective Measure 3D Garment height and circumference. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Measurement ▶ Linear/Circumference Garment Measure 3D Toolbar ▶ Linear Garment Measure / Circumference Garment Measure ### Operation #### Linear Garment Measure 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Measurement ▶ Linear Garment Measure 3D Toolbar ▶ Linear Garment Measure 2. Click the beginning point of the Linear Garment Measure on a 3D Garment once. → A green dot and rectangle appear. 3. While pressing Shift on the keyboard, click the endpoint of the measurement. → A vertical measurement with its length is now being created and displayed. #### Circumference Garment Measure 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Measurement ▶ Circumference Garment Measure 3D Toolbar ▶ Circumference Garment Measure 2. Click on an area to measure its circumference. → A circumference measurement with its value is now being created and displayed.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for accurately measuring the height and circumference of 3D garments using the Linear and Circumference Garment Measure tools.

title: Direct Positioning
content: ### Objective Activate Direct Positioning to click to easily arrange Patterns and OBJs. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Click 3D Pattern or OBJ ▶ ![Direct_Positioning.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438211305497) Direct Positioning ### Operation 1. Follow the path: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Click 3D Pattern or OBJ ▶ ![Direct_Positioning.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438211305497) Direct Positioning 2. Hover the mouse over a Garment or Avatar. → The selected Pattern or OBJ moves along with the mouse cursor. 3. Click to place the Pattern in the desired location. ※Note: When arranging Patterns, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to restrict Pattern rotation (ver4.0.0).
content_description: Learn how to easily arrange Patterns and OBJs using Direct Positioning in the 3D Toolbar for precise placement in your designs.

title: Show/Hide Sewing
content: ### Objective When Sewing Lines are too complicated, hide them for clear view as needed. ### Location 2D/3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Sewing ▶ Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) ▶ Hide Sewing (Selected)/ Show Sewing (All) ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Sewing ▶ Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) ▶ Hide Sewing (Selected)/ Show Sewing (All) → The selected Sewing Lines or all Sewing Lines show or disappear from the 2D and the 3D window.
content_description: This web page provides instructions on how to hide or show sewing lines in 2D and 3D views for a clearer workspace when sewing lines become too complicated.

title: Change Length
content: ### Objective Type in the segment length and edit Pattern. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern 2. Right click on the segment to be adjusted to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Change Length. → The Change Length window appears. 3. Enter the length of the segment and select the desired location. → The preview shows in the 2D window. 4. Click OK. → The segment length is changed accordingly. ※Note: If a line connected to the selected line is a curve, the curve point is moved according to the changed length. If the "Lock Curve Points" option is checked, only straight points can be moved. (ver MD10)
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for editing segment lengths in 2D patterns using the main menu and toolbar options.

title: Edit Topstitch
content: ### Objective Relocate or adjust length of Topstitches. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Topstitch ▶ Edit Topstitch 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Topstitch ### Operation #### Relocate Topstitch 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Topstitch ▶ Edit Topstitch 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Topstitch 2. Click on a topstitch to change its location. → The selected Topstitch is being highlighted. 3. Drag to a desired location. #### Adjust Topstitch Length 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Topstitch ▶ Edit Topstitch 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Topstitch 2. Click and drag one of the two end points of a Topstitch to adjust its length. → The selected Topstitch is now being adjusted.
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for relocating or adjusting the length of Topstitches in your design project.

title: Fold Seam Line
content: ### Objective Use this function to create an pressing effect on sewn parts of Patterns. ### Location Property Editor ▶ Fold Angle ### Operation 1. Click on Edit Sewing tool. 2. Select the seamline to change its fold angle. 3. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ Fold Angle 4. Adjust the value, in the range of 0~360˚. ※ Note: * The value of fold angle is in between 0° to 360°, 180° represents a flat state. The internal line is folded towards the front of the pattern as the fold angle is closer to 0˚, and is folded into the back of the pattern as the angle is closer to 360˚. * #### Fold Strength The intensity of the fold is able to be set by adjusting the value of Fold Strength. The higher the value, the closer the fold is to the set angle. When a jacket and its lining are sewn together, the sewn area inflates due to the default sewing angle and intensity values. In this case, sets the Fold Strength to 0 to flatten the sewn boundaries. * When the Sewing type is set as Turned, Fold Strength and Fold Angle cannot be modified (ver4.0.0).
content_description: This web page provides guidance on adjusting the fold angle and strength of seams in sewing patterns to achieve desired pressing effects.

title: Edit Curve Point
content: ### ### ### ### ### ### Objective Add and edit curve points on Pattern outlines and Internal Lines. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Curve Point 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Curve Point ### Operation **Add** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location 2. Click the desired position of a segment to add a curve point. Or, Right click on a segment to split the segment by a curve point (ver 7.1) **Split into Two Lines** | Adjust by entering the length of both lines which are divided by the right clicked point, or by entering the ratio. ---|--- **Split by Length** | Enter the number of segments the selected line should be divided into. You can change the direction in which a point is added to a start/opposite/center basis. **Uniform Split** | Enter the number of segments the line should be divided into. The line is equally divided accordingly. → A free curve point is created at the selected point. → When a free curve point is added to an Bezier curve, the curvarture is changed based on the free curve point. **Move** 1. Click and drag a curve point or press the arrow key on the keyboard to move. To enter Moved Distance, right click while click-and-dragging the Curve Point **Distance Moved** | Type in the how much a segment or a point is moved. ---|--- **X/ Y Axis** | Type in how much a point is moved on X/ Y-axis. This option does not appear for segments. ※ Note: * Moving multiple curve points at once is possible starting ver4.2.0 (ver4.2.0). The Transform pattern tool's selection box can now select patterns no matter the area it covers; by holding CTRL and clicking and dragging your mouse. (ver. 2024.0) * The Free Curve Point can be freely added and edited. The Free Curve Point can also be created by holding down the Ctrl key on the keyboard while drafting a Pattern with the Polygon tool. * When a Free Curve Point is added to an AI Bezier curve, its AI Bezier curve handles disappear and the curve is reshaped based on the added Free Curve Point.
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions for adding and editing curve points on pattern outlines and internal lines using the 2D Pattern editing tools.
